documentation.content:
The v2 aggregate trigger logged an error.

Why this one is watched by severity: onV2AnswerCreated runs with retry:true, so Eventarc redelivers failures for up to ~7 days. A crashing trigger does not drain, it accumulates — and every answer written meanwhile misses the aggregate, so the Mirror's world split silently stops moving while the app looks healthy.

Why severity is the right signal HERE and not everywhere: this trigger runs when a user answers, so an outage produces errors. The reveal scan is a cron, whose characteristic failure is not running at all — it is watched by absence instead (monitoring/scheduledDuelReveals-silent.json), because an error policy on a function that never executes stays green through the whole outage.

First response is containment, not a fix: deploy a no-op body so deliveries are acknowledged, then fix forward. Reverting alone leaves the backlog to replay against the old code. Replay itself is safe — v2_agg_events/{eventId} is checked inside the same transaction that increments counts, so redelivered events are no-ops rather than double counts.

Full runbook: docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, 'Rolling back a bad deploy'.
